articles.title: Ollie vs The Farmer's Dog 2026: The Prices Each Brand Actually Publishes, Per Meal vs Per Day
articles.description: Ollie vs The Farmer's Dog built only from the two brands' own pages, read 2026-09-26: The Farmer's Dog publishes one number - plans start at about $2 a day - while Ollie publishes $1.57 and $1.00 a meal plus a FAQ range of under $4 a day for small dogs and $8 a day on average. Different units, so they cannot be subtracted; each cell carries its official source.
articles.h1: Ollie vs The Farmer's Dog: what each brand publishes about price, checked 2026-09-26
articles.lede: Quick answer: the two brands do not publish the same kind of number, so a straight price-versus-price verdict does not exist on their own sites. The Farmer's Dog prints one figure - plans start at about $2/day, with delivery options mostly ranging from 1 week to 2 months of food and including free shipping. Ollie prints per-meal figures instead - Full Fresh Meals from $1.57 a meal, Half Fresh Plan from $1.00 a meal - and answers in per-day terms only inside its FAQ: food starts at less than four dollars a day for small dogs fed Ollie exclusively, and averages $8 a day. Neither brand prices your dog on a public page (Ollie uses its plan builder, The Farmer's Dog uses a questionnaire), so the numbers below are floors, not bills. Every line carries its official source and a check date of 2026-09-26.

rows.label: Starting price the brand prints
cells: 'Starting at $1.57 a meal' for Full Fresh Meals (Premium) and 'Starting at $1.00 a meal' for the Half Fresh Plan (budget friendly). Both are floor prices: your dog's plan is priced inside Ollie's plan builder.
'Plans start at about $2/day.' The exact plan and price depend on age, weight, activity and recipe choice, and The Farmer's Dog shows them after you fill out its questionnaire.

rows.label: Unit of that price
cells: Per meal on the public page. Its per-day figures live in the FAQ instead: food starts at less than four dollars a day for small dogs fed Ollie exclusively, and averages $8 a day.
Per day. The FAQ does not print a per-meal price anywhere, so there is no Ollie-style per-meal figure to compare against.

rows.label: What your first delivery contains
cells: A starter box with the first two weeks of food plus a welcome kit - a scoop and a puptainer for storage.
Delivery options mostly range from 1 week to 2 months of food, and each plan is customized to your dog's needs.

rows.label: Shipping cost
cells: Free delivery: the Meal Plans page title reads 'Dog Meal Plans | Free Delivery | Ollie'. No minimum order is printed on the page.
The FAQ says delivery options 'include free shipping'. No minimum order is printed either.

rows.label: Where it ships
cells: The continental United States - Ollie says it is unable to ship to Alaska or Hawaii at this time.
The 48 contiguous states.

rows.label: Commitment and how you cancel
cells: Subscription only - Ollie says it is currently a subscription-based service, so you cannot order without subscribing. Cancelling happens on the website account (not in the app): My Plan > My Info > Subscriptions > Cancel Subscription, once per dog; Ollie also prints a cancellation line, +1 650-405-3420, 9am-8pm ET Mon-Fri and 10am-7pm ET Sat.
'Yes, you can easily pause, cancel or reactivate your subscription anytime' from the Customer Account.

rows.label: When the money leaves your account
cells: Three days before the package ships; once the order charges, Ollie says it cannot be edited or altered.
An email notice before each order is billed and shipped; the FAQ does not print how many days before shipment that is.

rows.label: Storage once it arrives
cells: Freezer up to 6 months unopened; thaw in the refrigerator for 24 hours, then the food is good for up to 4 days - keep it in the puptainer with the lid on.
Keep it in a refrigerator or freezer, and only feed packs that arrive frozen or very cold (still below 40°F). Instant Fresh is shelf-stable and does not need refrigerating.

rows.label: Recipes and product lines
cells: Five recipes on the Meal Plans page - Beef (marked POPULAR), Chicken, Lamb, Turkey and Pork - across Full Fresh and Half Fresh plans; Ollie's FAQ also lists a Baked food that can be mixed with fresh.

Two serving styles: Fresh (gently cooked, quickly frozen) and Instant Fresh (shelf-stable), plus Treats. Proteins are beef, chicken, turkey and pork, formulated to AAFCO standards by on-staff board-certified veterinary nutritionists.

faqs.q: Which brand publishes a per-day starting price?
faqs.a: Only The Farmer's Dog. Its FAQ says 'Plans start at about $2/day'. Ollie publishes per-meal starting prices on its Meal Plans page ($1.57 Full Fresh, $1.00 Half Fresh) and gives per-day figures only inside its FAQ - under $4 a day for small dogs fed Ollie exclusively, averaging $8 a day.

faqs.q: Is Ollie cheaper than The Farmer's Dog?
faqs.a: Their own pages do not answer that, and neither do we. The two publish different units (per meal versus per day), each prices your dog individually through its own tool, and neither brand publishes a head-to-head figure for the same dog. Anyone quoting a single winner is doing arithmetic the brands themselves do not do.

faqs.q: How much does Ollie cost per day?
faqs.a: Ollie's own FAQ says its food starts at less than four dollars per day for small dogs who are exclusively fed Ollie, and averages $8 per day. It also says prices vary based on the size of your dog and the size of their portions, so the average is its own figure, not a quote for your dog.

faqs.q: How much does The Farmer's Dog cost per day?
faqs.a: Its FAQ says plans start at about $2/day, and that your exact plan and price depend on age, weight, activity and recipe choice. The exact pricing options appear after you fill out the questionnaire.

faqs.q: Do either of them charge for shipping?
faqs.a: Both advertise it as free. Ollie's Meal Plans page title reads 'Dog Meal Plans | Free Delivery | Ollie'; The Farmer's Dog says its delivery options include free shipping. Neither page prints a minimum order for it.

faqs.q: Where do they ship?
faqs.a: Ollie ships to pups in the continental United States and says it cannot ship to Alaska or Hawaii at this time. The Farmer's Dog ships to the 48 contiguous states.

faqs.q: Can you cancel whenever you want?
faqs.a: Both say yes, with different mechanics. The Farmer's Dog: pause, cancel or reactivate anytime from your Customer Account. Ollie: cancel from your account on its website (not the app), one dog at a time, or call +1 650-405-3420 - cancelling turns off auto-renewal and does not affect orders already in progress.

faqs.q: How do you store the food when it arrives?
faqs.a: Ollie: freezer up to 6 months unopened, 24 hours to thaw in the fridge, then up to 4 days to serve. The Farmer's Dog: keep it refrigerated or frozen and only feed packs that arrive frozen or very cold, still below 40°F - its Instant Fresh line is shelf-stable and needs no refrigeration.

faqs.q: Is there a first-order discount?
faqs.a: On 2026-09-26 both brands advertised one: The Farmer's Dog showed '50% off your first purchase', and Ollie's pages showed 50% at 19:06 (UTC+8) and 70% later the same evening. Ollie's banner figure changed within minutes of our check, so confirm the current offer and its terms on the brand's site before ordering.

faqs.q: What is in the first delivery?
faqs.a: Ollie's starter box is the first two weeks of food plus a welcome kit with a scoop and a puptainer. The Farmer's Dog's delivery options mostly range from 1 week to 2 months of food, with the amount customized to your dog.

articles.disclaimer: Assembled only from ollie.com and thefarmersdog.com pages read on 2026-09-26 (UTC+8) - no third-party comparison site, no affiliate quote, no invented price. Both brands publish starting prices and per-day statements rather than quotes for your dog, so treat every figure here as a floor; promos change without notice (Ollie's first-box banner differed between two readings on the same evening). Re-read the official page before you order.

blocks.html:
This page is a read-out, not an opinion. On 2026-09-26 (UTC+8) we fetched Ollie's Meal Plans page in raw HTML at 19:06, opened The Farmer's Dog's FAQ and Ollie's FAQ in a real browser at 19:10, and re-read Ollie's homepage at 19:21 - then opened Ollie's FAQ answers one question at a time (cost, billing, cancellation, storage, shipping), because the answers are loaded on click and do not appear in the page source.

What that produced: one per-day number from The Farmer's Dog, two per-meal numbers plus two per-day numbers from Ollie, and a set of terms (shipping, cancellation, storage, billing) that are simply printed differently by each brand. Where a brand does not publish something, the cell says so instead of guessing.

Deliberately excluded: every third-party comparison table, every crowd-sourced price, and every conversion between units that the brands themselves never print.

blocks.h2: The exclusive bit: each brand publishes the number the other one does not
blocks.html:
This is the whole comparison in one line: only The Farmer's Dog publishes a per-day starting price, and only Ollie publishes per-meal starting prices. That is not a stylistic quirk - it changes what you can honestly calculate.

Ollie gives you $1.57 and $1.00 but no official meals-per-day figure, so the public pages never multiply them out; its per-day answer lives in a separate FAQ entry ($8 average, under $4 for small dogs). The Farmer's Dog gives you about $2 a day and never prints a per-meal number anywhere on its FAQ. So a reader who types 'Ollie vs The Farmer's Dog price' into a search box will find sites doing the multiplication for them; the brands do not.

The terms diverge in the same pattern. Ollie pins down the mechanics to the day (charged three days before shipping, freezer life of 6 months unopened, 4 days once thawed, cancel on the website but not the app) while The Farmer's Dog keeps it loose (pause, cancel, reactivate anytime; food below 40°F on arrival; delivery from 1 week to 2 months). Neither is wrong - they are just different disclosures, and both are printed in the sources linked beside each row.

faqs.q: What is in the first box?
faqs.a: Ollie says the starter box contains the first two weeks of food plus a welcome kit - a handy scoop and a puptainer to store the food.

articles.disclaimer: Built only from Ollie's own pages (ollie.com/meal-plans, ollie.com/faqs and ollie.com) read on 2026-09-26 (UTC+8), including the FAQ answers that only load when you click each question. Ollie publishes starting prices, averages and a first-box banner rather than a quote for your dog, and the banner figure differed between two readings the same evening - so re-read the official page before ordering, and treat any per-day multiplication you do yourself as your own arithmetic, not Ollie's.

blocks.html:
Ollie's cost-per-day answer is not on its pricing page - it sits behind a click on the FAQ. On 2026-09-26 (UTC+8) we fetched the Meal Plans page in raw HTML at 19:06, then opened ollie.com/faqs in a real browser at 19:10 and clicked through the answers one by one (How much does Ollie cost, When am I charged for each order, Can I order Ollie without subscribing, What's included in my starter box, How do I cancel my subscription, Can I freeze the food, Where do you ship), and re-read the homepage at 19:21.

The finding is that Ollie publishes two different units and never converts them. Per-meal prices live on the Meal Plans page; per-day figures live in the FAQ. Nowhere does Ollie print how many meals its $8-a-day average assumes, so this page does not do that multiplication either.

Deliberately left out: any estimated monthly bill, any breed-by-breed price table (Ollie does not publish one), and any figure from a third-party review or coupon site.

blocks.h2: What Ollie actually tells you about the bill
blocks.html:
Strip the marketing out and Ollie's public pages disclose five money facts: two per-meal starting prices, two per-day statements, and a billing rule. The starter box is your first two weeks of food, your card is charged three days before the box ships, and after that charge the order is locked. Delivery is advertised free in the page title, and the plan is a subscription you cancel on the website rather than in the app.

One thing worth flagging because it cost us two fetches: the first-box banner is not stable. On 2026-09-26 the same site served '50% off your first box' at 19:06 and '70% off your first box' at 19:21. If you are pricing Ollie, the discount you see when you start the plan builder is the only one that counts.
